dataset.description: This dataset is generated within the AQUASERV TNA project investigating the role of the endocannabinoid system in the regulation of feeding behaviour and appetite in rainbow trout. The dataset includes behavioural observations, feed intake measurements, plasma metabolite data, gene expression results. The purpose of the dataset is to improve understanding of the physiological and molecular mechanisms underlying appetite regulation in fish and to support future scientific publications and research in aquaculture nutrition and fish physiology.

format:
The project will generate several types of research data, including behavioural observations from video recordings, feed intake measurements, plasma metabolite data, gene expression data (qPCR), protein expression data (Western blot), endocannabinoid quantification (HPLC-MS/MS), immunohistochemistry images, and associated experimental metadata.

Data will be stored in standard digital formats, including:

Video files (.mp4)
Spreadsheets and tabular data (.xlsx, .csv)
Images (.tiff, .png)
Laboratory records and documentation (.pdf, .docx)

These formats were selected to ensure long-term accessibility, interoperability, and compatibility with commonly used scientific software.

Yes, a temporary embargo may be applied to derived datasets to allow time for scientific publication of results. The embargo would typically last until acceptance of the related publication or up to 12–24 months after data collection, whichever comes first. No embargo is foreseen for intellectual property purposes.

The embargo will be defined by the Principal Investigator at the time of data submission and recorded in the repository. It will be lifted automatically by the repository at the end of the embargo period, or earlier upon confirmation of publication.

dmp.description:
The TNA project investigates the role of the endocannabinoid system in the regulation of feeding behaviour and appetite in rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss). Fish are exposed to pharmacological blockade of CB1 receptors using rimonabant, and behavioural, physiological, molecular, and biochemical responses are assessed.

The project will generate behavioural data from video recordings, feed intake measurements, plasma metabolite data (glucose, lactate, NEFA, and triglycerides), gene expression data obtained by qPCR. Associated metadata, experimental records, and statistical analysis files will also be generated and stored.
